paper.title_en: Sector-resolved Bayesian model averaging for DESI-Era cosmology
paper.abstract_en: We present a quotient-space Bayesian formulation for DESI-Era anomaly interpretation. Given a pattern-labeled catalog with map <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, the induced posterior <math display="inline"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, sector inclusion probabilities <math display="inline"><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></math>, coactivation probabilities <math display="inline"><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></math>, and grouped Bayes factors <math display="inline"><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> are exact summaries over predeclared physical activation events. Pairwise comparisons such as <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>CDM</mi></math> versus <math display="inline"><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mi>CDM</mi></math> remain ordinary Bayes-factor tests between specified families; the quotient construction addresses the coarser question of which physical sector carries posterior support when different sectors are represented by unequal numbers of catalog elements. We derive a sector-resolved DESI-CMB-SN likelihood specification for late-time background, early-time ruler, supernova calibration, perturbation, and gravitational-wave propagation sectors. The construction includes an Alcock-Paczynski/isotropic-scale BAO decomposition, a pure-ruler projection, analytic marginalization of low-rank supernova calibration modes, Fisher-normalized sector priors, inactive-sector leakage tests, log-evidence uncertainty propagation, and prior/sector-partition diagnostics. The result is a quantitative procedure for reporting model-comparison support at the level of physically interpretable sectors.
